text:
ben.s: Heads up — ACME reported a sudden p95/p99 latency spike ~12:15 PST, affects their dedicated pool. They see request queuing and occasional 502s. Logs show a lot of auth rejections mixed in.
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: tenant=acme corp, p99_latency=1.9s (+700ms), queued_requests=420, auth_fail_rate=0.6% (rolling 5m)
alice.r: Thanks. Any repro curl or request pattern from ACME? can we narrow to a route/model?
ben.s: They sent a repro: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":512}'` repeatedly from ~20 hosts. They said they ramped traffic up to test blue/green.
carol_m: That sounds like a classic admission-control + auth thundering pattern. If many hosts send identical tokens but some tokens are expired, auth lookups can slow admission. Do we have recent worker saturation stats for the tenant?
ops-bot: metric snapshot: worker_cpu=92%, kv-cache_hit=31%, admission_drop_rate=18%, inflight_per_worker=98
alice.r: kv-cache hit that low is suspicious. Could be cold prefix caches due to many different connection IDs. Also admission_drop 18% explains queueing.
ben.s: Customer says spikes started right after they rotated their deploy and started retrying failures aggressively. We should treat this as both an auth and concurrency storm.
sam.k: Quick mitigation options: 1) enable Tenant Holdoff rule (temporary reduce concurrency for ACME) 2) bump admission window for their pool 3) enable model fallback to smaller model to reduce token compute. Which can we do fastest?
alice.r: Number 1 is quickest. I can flip a holdoff to cap concurrent requests to 32 for the tenant. That should reduce worker pressure and let auth backends catch up. I'll also add a canary rule to prioritize non-retry requests.
carol_m: Also recommend reducing auth lookup cost: switch ACME to cached token validation for 60s TTL for the next 15m while we stabilize. Ops-team needs to coordinate with Auth service.
ben.s: I applied holdoff + prioritized non-retries. Patch: `rbacctl set-tenant-limit --tenant acme --concurrency 32 --reason "emergency holdoff 2026-03-17"`
ops-bot: action logged: set-tenant-limit by alice.r (trace id abc123)
alice.r: After flip: queued_requests=68, p99_latency=860ms, worker_cpu=74%
sam.k: Nice. That's a clear improvement. Can we also throttle retries at the gateway so clients don't hammer on 5xx? Add short-lived `Retry-After` header or return 429 instead of 502 for over-limit.
carol_m: We already have gateway config — I pushed a policy change: `gatewayctl set-retry-policy --tenant acme --mode fail-fast --max-retries 0` — should take effect immediately.
ben.s: Customer confirms reduced retry rate from their side after we told them to pause automated ramp. They will rotate their token issuance to avoid expired tokens flooding auth.
alice.r: For longer-term: we should add a tenant-specific auth cache and an admission knob that watches auth latency. If auth latency > 200ms, admission should tighten gracefully. Filing a ticket.
ben.s: Filed infra ticket INFRA-5532 with notes + graphs.
ops-bot: note: incident sensitivity = medium, sla-impact = partial degradation (ACME only)
carol_m: Before we close: need to capture repro steps for SRE postmortem. Ben, can you paste a short reproducer and attach request IDs?
ben.s: Repro: run 50 hosts concurrently with this small loop, token rotation every 60s: ```for i in {1..50}; do while true; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"x","max_tokens":8}'; sleep 0.2; done & done``` Attached sample request_ids: req_98a1, req_b3c4, req_ef12.
alice.r: Adding these to the postmortem. Follow-ups: (1) default retry-fencing for tenant-created spikes, (2) add auth-latency circuit for admission control, (3) tenant-level backoff guidance in support runbook.
sam.k: I'll send the support note to ACME summarizing actions and recommended client-side fixes (:email:).
ben.s: Customer thanks us, will monitor and report if anything else. Closing thread after 2h observation window if stable. :white_check_mark:
